### The Issue

The `CS0117` build error occurs because recent versions of the `Testcontainers` NuGet package removed the static `TestcontainersSettings.Logger` property. Logging configuration has been moved away from global settings and is now handled on a per-container basis via the builder API.

### The Fix

To resolve this, you need to remove the static logger assignments and instead use the `.WithLogger()` extension method directly on your `PostgreSqlBuilder` instances.

**1. Update `PostgreSqlFixture.cs**`
In `MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tests/PostgreSqlFixture.cs`, remove the `TestcontainersSettings.Logger = NullLogger.Instance;` assignment. Update your builder to look like this:

```csharp
_container = new PostgreSqlBuilder(PostgreSqlImage)
    .WithDatabase("myrestaurant")
    .WithUsername("myrestaurant")
    .WithPassword("myrestaurant")
    .WithLogger(NullLogger.Instance)
    .Build();

```

**2. Update `RestaurantHarness.cs**`
Similarly, in `MyRestaurant.EndToEnd.Tests/Harness/RestaurantHarness.cs`, remove the `TestcontainersSettings.Logger = NullLogger.Instance;` assignment and update the builder chain:

```csharp
_container = new PostgreSqlBuilder(PostgreSqlImage)
    .WithDatabase("postgres")
    .WithUsername("myrestaurant")
    .WithPassword("myrestaurant")
    .WithLogger(NullLogger.Instance)
    .Build();

```

Once you move `NullLogger.Instance` into the builder configuration for both files, your tests will compile successfully.

Slice 70 change manifest
Slice 70 — what's wrong and how it's fixed
Your diagnosis and your fixture fix were both correct. Testcontainers moved logger configuration off the static TestcontainersSettings.Logger and onto the builder before 4.14.0, the version Directory.Packages.props pins. I verified this against the library source at tag 4.14.0: TestcontainersSettings has no Logger member (also absent at 4.13.0 and 4.12.0), AbstractBuilder.WithLogger(ILogger) is the replacement, and Init() seeds every builder with ConsoleLogger.Instance — which is the noise you were silencing.

What was left broken was the gate:

Fact 1 keyed on "TestcontainersSettings.Logger =", which your fix had to delete. → rewritten to key on .WithLogger(, and made per builder chain rather than per file.
Fact 2 asserted the position of a global assignment. There is no global any more, so there is no position. Under F-41 (a rule whose subject has ceased to exist is deleted, not weakened) it is deleted — which is what you tried. What stopped that being the fix was §16.4's assertion count, which this slice moves in the same commit.
So: 1322 observed → 1321, and §16.4's paragraph for the class goes 2 assertions → 1.

The surviving fact is stronger than the one it replaces: two builders in one file with one silencer now fails (the old file-level Contains passed it), and a builder with no .Build() after it is reported rather than treated as satisfied. It keys on the call, not the value, so the "swap NullLogger for a warning-threshold logger" veto still works.

Emulated, all five planted defects reported: silencer deleted from the fixture; deleted from the harness instead; second unsilenced builder added; .Build() renamed away; and the pre-slice tree with the static assignment, which reproduces your exact failure. §16.4 census re-emulated green at 47 counted, floor 37, no disagreements.

Two riders, both caused by the same finding:

Both fixtures drop using DotNet.Testcontainers.Configurations; — TestcontainersSettings was the only thing either took from it.
Directory.Packages.props loses "as resolved on 2026-08-02" (F-77: three annotations in that same file already contradicted it) and gains a note that 4.x configures the logger per builder.
Files changed — all full files, nothing to delete, nothing to git add:
